Using the i915 PM wiring in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915`:

## PCI PM callbacks reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

The system-suspend callbacks are wired to the same function:

```text
PCI PM .suspend
    └── i915_pm_suspend(dev)

PCI PM .freeze
    └── i915_pm_suspend(dev)

PCI PM .poweroff
    └── i915_pm_suspend(dev)
```

The common suspend path is:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *dev)
    └── pci_dev = to_pci_dev(dev)
        └── dev_priv = pci_get_drvdata(pci_dev)
            └── i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv)
                ├── intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
                ├── i915_gem_suspend(...)
                ├── intel_gt_suspend(...)
                ├── intel_uncore_suspend(...)
                └── other display/GEM/GT suspend handling
```

The exact subordinate operations are conditionally platform- and configuration-dependent, but the path relevant to the requested display flow is always:

```text
PCI .suspend/.freeze/.poweroff
    → i915_pm_suspend()
    → i915_drm_suspend()
    → intel_display_suspend()
```

The callbacks that do **not** reach `i915_pm_suspend` are:

```text
PCI .resume
    └── i915_pm_resume()

PCI .thaw
    └── i915_pm_resume()

PCI .restore
    └── i915_pm_resume()

PCI .runtime_suspend
    └── i915_pm_runtime_suspend()

PCI .runtime_resume
    └── i915_pm_runtime_resume()
```

Relevant implementation and declarations are in:

- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.h`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_driver.c`
- `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_driver.h`

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the system-suspend callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend` also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

The two paths are separate:

```text
System PM:
    .suspend/.freeze/.poweroff
        → i915_pm_suspend()
        → i915_drm_suspend()

Runtime PM:
    .runtime_suspend
        → i915_pm_runtime_suspend()
        → runtime-PM-specific suspend handling
```

Thus:

| PCI PM callback | Reaches `i915_pm_suspend` | Calls `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` |
|---|---:|---:|
| `.suspend` | Yes | No |
| `.freeze` | Yes | No |
| `.poweroff` | Yes | No |
| `.resume` | No | No |
| `.thaw` | No | No |
| `.restore` | No | No |
| `.runtime_suspend` | No; it is the runtime callback itself | N/A—this is the callback |
| `.runtime_resume` | No | No |

## `dev_priv` data flow

The PCI PM callback receives a generic `struct device *`. The i915 private device is recovered from the PCI device's driver data:

```text
struct device *dev
    │
    ├── to_pci_dev(dev)
    │       └── struct pci_dev *pdev
    │
    └── pci_get_drvdata(pdev)
            └── struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
```

That pointer is then passed unchanged through the suspend helpers:

```c
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *dev)
{
        struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(dev);
        struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = pci_get_drvdata(pdev);

        return i915_drm_suspend(dev_priv);
```
